paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average change percentage across multiple turns, categorized by the initial answer type. The x-axis is labeled “Turn Number” and uses a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels at integer values. The y-axis is labeled “Average Change Percentage (%)” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 50, with tick labels at 10% intervals. The first line, colored red with circular markers and a solid line style, begins at approximately 5% at turn 1 and increases to approximately 25% at turn 2, then rises to approximately 33% at turn 3, before climbing sharply to approximately 48% at turn 4. From turn 4 to turn 7, the line remains relatively steady, fluctuating between approximately 48% and 50%.  The second line, colored gray with no markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 8% at turn 1, declines to around 6% at turn 2, then rises to around 9% at turn 3, after which it remains relatively constant, fluctuating between approximately 10% and 12% from turn 3 through turn 7.
